description:
Run shell commands on the OS/shell/backend named in your environment section. The working directory, files and exported variables persist between calls: activate a virtualenv or export once, not before every command.

Use read_file, search_files, patch and write_file instead of cat/head/tail, grep/find/ls, sed/awk and echo/heredoc. Output is auto-truncated with the full text saved to a file; never pipe through head/tail to shorten it.

Foreground (default) returns as soon as the command finishes. To wait a fixed time, run the wait in the foreground; never background a sleep or polling loop. Health-check a background server in a separate call and manage jobs with process_manage. A background job has exactly ONE reader: decide before you launch — either you read the result (leave notify unset, then process_manage(action='wait')) or the completion notification delivers it (notify=true, then STOP; the notification starts a NEW TURN, so do not also poll). When a command changes directory, trust the result's "cwd" instead of prefixing later commands with cd.
name: terminal

background.description: Only for commands that must keep running after this call returns; returns a session_id. A background job has exactly ONE reader, and you must decide which BEFORE you launch: either you read the result yourself (leave notify unset, then use process_manage(action='wait')) or the completion notification delivers it to you (set notify=true and then STOP — do not also poll it). notify is not a free message: it starts a NEW TURN, and you cannot un-arm it once launched.

heartbeat.description: With background=true: also notify every N seconds (min 60) with new output; quiet ticks are skipped. For bounded jobs you must react to mid-run, never servers. Implies notify=true; 0 = off.

notify.description: With background=true. A background job has exactly ONE reader, and you must decide which BEFORE you launch. true: one notification on exit — but that notification STARTS A NEW TURN (it is not a passive message: the agent wakes and re-reads its context), and you cannot un-arm it once launched. Use true ONLY if you will NOT read the result yourself: then STOP after launching and let the notification BE the delivery, and do not also poll it. If you WILL read the output (or wait for it) yourself, leave this unset — arming it as well delivers the same result twice, once by you and once as a new turn. Otherwise the job runs silently. ['pattern', ...]: notify when a line matches, only for one-shot readiness on processes that never exit; rate-limited. Omit for servers/daemons.

persist_on_release.description: With background=true: survive session end, /new, compression and other cleanup (not host exit). Only for jobs the user explicitly wants to outlive the conversation.

pty.description: With background=true: pseudo-terminal for interactive CLIs (REPLs, coding agents); drive it with process_manage write/submit. Local backend only.

timeout.description: Max seconds (default 180, foreground max 600). Finishing early returns at once, so set it generously. Above 600s the command runs as a tracked background process with notify_on_complete=true (the result says so; do not re-run it).

workdir.description: Absolute working directory for this command only.
